source.title: Normalization Layer Per-Example Gradients are Sufficient to Predict Gradient Noise Scale in Transformers
source.authors: Gavia Gray; Aman Tiwari; Shane Bergsma; Joel Hestness

page_placements.theme: Capacity effects depend on data, architecture and training

record.tranche_reason: The study measures gradient noise scale and its use in batch-size scheduling, but does not measure the training-to-test gap or held-out generalization named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study varies learning rate and batch size and measures GNS (Figure 6); these results do not measure generalization. Its batch-size schedule reports training loss and tokens saved, not held-out error. Background references to prior work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures gradient noise scale, computational overhead, and training-loss improvements from batch scheduling. These do not test V5's held-out performance claim or V7's magnitude-aware sharpness claim. Appendix C.1 reports validation loss across model sizes, but varies token budgets at fixed compute and does not test widening beyond zero training error as required by V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that normalization-layer gradient statistics provide a practical estimate of total Transformer GNS with zero throughput overhead, enabling batch scheduling; the abstract reports an 18% training-time reduction in their case study.
record.recipe_differences: Measures per-example gradients and GNS in Transformer language models; it does not test the original generalization methods or outcomes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: GNS responded predictably to learning-rate changes, while batch-size changes did not produce the predicted response (Section 4.1).

fits_no_version.finding: In the 111M language model, learning-rate changes produce the predicted GNS response, while batch-size changes do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The predicted dependence of GNS on the batch-size-to-learning-rate ratio does not fully transfer to this Transformer setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.1 reports minimum validation losses of 3.246, 3.230, and 3.238 for 70M, 111M, and 161M models, respectively, with token budgets adjusted to hold compute fixed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Among these three model sizes, the intermediate size achieves the lowest validation loss under the tested fixed compute budget.

record.problems: Figure 6 provides the intervention traces without numeric values in the text. The study reports no held-out generalization measure for these interventions.
record.rows_left_out: The batch-size schedule case study in Section 5.2 reports training loss and tokens saved to reach the same loss, not test or held-out error, so it does not qualify as a result on the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization and local connectivity.
Held-out optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove its penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error and their dependence on data size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Test accuracy after removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 9 reports training loss, not held-out loss. Figure 10 does report validation loss, so the exclusion rests on its different experimental question rather than a complete absence of held-out measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and their test errors.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance and the effects of tuning or optimizer changes.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: 111M parameter language model
rows.operation_detail: Measured GNS while varying the learning rate from the same training point.

conditions.value: learning rate varied; exact values figure only

rows.note: The text says GNS reacts predictably to learning-rate changes; precise values are only in the figure.
rows.check: The reported learning-rate response concerns GNS, which cannot establish any claim version's effect. The subject and qualitative finding are correct.

rows.subject: 111M parameter language model
rows.operation_detail: Measured GNS while varying batch size from the same training point.

conditions.value: batch size varied; exact values figure only

rows.note: The authors state that batch-size changes do not have the effect predicted by the theory.
rows.check: GNS cannot establish any claim version's effect. Failure of the predicted GNS response also does not establish that batch size has no effect; 'absent' overstates the source.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Related work discusses batch size, optimizer differences and sharp minima; the study neither tests nor uses the specified generalization findings.

tranche.reason: GNS estimation and batch scheduling measure training efficiency, without testing the versions' generalization outcomes. Appendix C.1 varies model size and token budget at fixed compute, without testing V2's interpolation condition.

source_check.notes: The pack lists no rows or verdicts to check. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate; the abstract reports an 18% training-time reduction.

statements.correction: Appendix C.1: token budgets adjusted to keep total FLOPs constant; model sizes 70M, 111M, 161M; Figure 10 minimum validation losses 3.246, 3.230, 3.238; prose identifies 111M as lowest, establishing 111M = 3.230; remaining model-to-loss assignments unverified.
statements.problem: Figure 10 contains all three losses, but the extracted text loses the curve associations needed to verify the 70M and 161M assignments.
